（豊田市坂上町、2019年（令和元年）11月）]] 六所山は古来より[[猿投山]]・[[本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|本宮山]]と共に[[三河国]]三霊山のひとつとされ、山自体が[[神体]]とされて[[大山積神]]（オオヤマツミ）など6柱の祭神が奉祀されていた『松平町誌』：758-759ページ。現在でも字金姓の小台地にたたずむ一の鳥居は、六所山を遙拝するのに最も適した場所にあり、古代、この地に最初期の遙拝所が建てられたものとも推察し得る『坂上町誌』：10ページ。後に[[社殿]]の築造という[[仏教]]文化に由来する概念が国内に浸透し、六所山山頂にも社殿が築かれることになるのは遅くとも[[平安時代]]末期頃と考えられており、上宮近辺で平安時代から[[室町時代]]にかけての[[土器]]（かわらけ）片が発見されるのは、この地でこの時代に[[祭祀]]が行われていたことを裏付けるものである『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ。なお、[[1604]]（[[慶長]]9年）の『慶長検地帳』には鳥居下という地名がみられることから一の鳥居がこの時期にすでに築造されていたと推定されるが、建立そのものの時期はよく分かっていない。鳥居の両際には長らくマツの巨木が立ちそびえており、2本とも[[樹齢]]500年以上と言われていたが、[[1959]]（[[昭和]]34年）[[9月]]に上陸した[[伊勢湾台風]]によって倒れている『坂上町誌』：88ページ。 一帯はかつては[[松平郷]]といい、[[松平氏]]（[[徳川氏]]）発祥の地である。[[1377]]（[[永和 (日本)|永和]]3年・[[天授 (日本)|天授]]3年）[[8月19日 (旧暦)|8月19日]]、松平宗家初代[[松平親氏|松平太郎左衛門親氏]]が[[Mutsu Province |奥州]]より鹽竈（しおがま）六所明神（[[鹽竈神社]]の六所宮の神）を六所山に勧請した上で奉祀したとされる。それまで「吉木山」「蜂ケ峰山」などとされていた山名が、以降六所山と呼ばれるようになる。[[産土神]]として奉拝されていた[[大山祇神]]はその社地を譲って北東の蜂ケ峰に遷され、以来「隠居神様」と呼ばれながら六所神社[[摂社]]の八ケ峰神社として存続することになる一方、新たに祀られた[[客人神]]の本殿は芳樹宮と名付けられ、六所大明神と称されて、松平氏・徳川氏の[[氏神]]として歴代当主の崇拝を受けていくことになる『松平町誌』：759ページ。早くも[[1474]]（[[応仁]]元年）には松平宗家第4代[[松平親忠]]が、[[1520]]（[[永正]]元年）には松平宗家第5代[[松平長親]]が社殿の再建に取り組んでいる。[[1527]]（[[大永]]7年）12月には野火で社殿が全焼したが、このとき松平長親と松平宗家第6代[[松平信忠]]は連署の上、松平家一門に対して殿舎再建への[[寄進]]を依頼している。なお、下宮は六所山南麓にある槙ケ田和村（現豊田市[[花沢町]]）に鎮座していたのを現在地に移し、当地を宮口村と名付けて社領としたのも松平長親だとする伝承が残っている『坂上町誌』：245ページ。[[1542]]（[[天文 (元号)|天文]]11年）に松平宗家第8代[[松平広忠]]に[[嫡子]]竹千代が誕生した際に礼拝がなされたといわれる高宮村（現[[岡崎市]][[明大寺町]]）の[[六所神社 (岡崎市)|六所神社]]に対し、竹千代長じて[[岡崎城]]城主となった[[徳川家康]]は、[[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku]]年間（[[1558]] - [[1570]]）に六所山六所大明神の祭神6柱のうち3柱を勧請し、遷座したという『坂上町誌』：246ページ。ただし岡崎市誌によれば、松平広忠寄進状などの史料より[[1546]]（天文15年）以前にはすでに遷座していたことがうかがわれる『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ。 {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikauji, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|松平親氏像
（豊田市[[松平町 (豊田市)|松平町]]、2019年（令和元年）8月） Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|徳川家康像
（[[狩野探幽]]画、[[大阪城]]天守閣蔵） }} [[1590]]（[[天正]]18年）の徳川家康[[関東]]移封の後は岡崎城城主[[田中吉政]]の支配下に入り、[[寺社領]]の没収を受けるが、[[1602]]（慶長7年）に徳川家康より高20石の大明神初穂料を下賜される。[[江戸時代]]に入ると、[[1617]]（[[元和 (日本)|元和]]3年）には[[松平太郎左衛門家]]第8代[[松平由重]]によって本殿が造営されるのと同時に[[玄米]]4石7斗8升3合が例祭料・灯明料として宮口村高より免引され『松平町誌』：760ページ、[[1638]]（[[寛永]]15年）には松平太郎左衛門家第10代[[松平重和]]によって再び本殿が造営され、[[1667]]（[[寛文]]7年）・[[1683]]（[[天和 (日本)|天和]]3年）・[[1686]]（[[貞享]]4年）には[[奥殿藩]][[大給松平家]]初代[[松平乗次]]によって堂宇が再建・改修され、[[1736]]（[[元文]]元年）から翌年にかけては奥殿藩大給松平家第4代[[松平盈乗]]による堂宇の再建、灯明料として玄米2石4斗の寄進、例祭料として7斗8升3合の免引などがあり、[[1779]]（[[安永 (元号)|安永]]8年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第5代[[松平乗穏]]による堂宇の造営『松平町誌』：761ページ、[[1790]]（[[寛政]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第7代[[松平乗尹]]による堂宇の造営、奥殿藩大給松平家第7代[[松平乗尹]]による堂宇の造営、[[1849]]（[[嘉永]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第9代[[松平乗利]]による下宮における[[不動一宇]]の造営、[[1858]]（[[安政]]5年）と[[1861]]（[[文久]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第10代松平乗謨及び松平太郎左衛門家第16代[[松平頼載]]によって本殿の再興・修復、鳥居の再興が行われるなど、徳川家・松平家一門、とりわけ宮口村領主である大給松平家と松平郷を領した松平太郎左衛門家による厚遇ぶりには枚挙の暇がない。 [[1873]]（[[明治]]6年）、六所大明神から'''六所神社'''と改称する。旧社格は[[郷社]]で、[[1917]]（[[大正]]6年）には御料林となっていた六所山社有林の払い下げが許可され、翌[[1918]]（大正7年）から[[1920]]（大正9年）にかけて下宮の拝殿及び祭文殿が再建、[[1921]]（大正10年）には県社に昇格している。現在は愛知県[[神社庁]]に属し、[[登記]]名を[[宗教法人]]六所神社としている『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ。 == 主な祭典行事 == * [[1月1日]]：[[歳旦祭]] * [[2月11日]]：紀元祭 * [[2月17日]]：[[祈年祭]]、秋葉神社祭、山の神祭 * [[6月30日]]：[[大祓]] * [[7月25日]]：八ヶ峰神社祭 * [[9月1日]]：二百十日祭、熱田祭 * [[9月22日]]：神迎え神事・前日祭 * [[9月23日]]：[[例祭]]・神送り神事 * [[11月23日]]：[[新嘗祭]] * [[12月31日]]：大祓・除夜祭 * 毎月1日：[[月次祭]] == 境内社 == * 八ヶ峰神社（上宮）：大山祇神（通称：「隠居神様」） * 秋葉神社（下宮）：軻遇突智神 == その他 == === 六所神社の舞台 === [[File:Rokusho Jinja Stage 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|六所神社舞台
（2019年（令和元年）11月）]] 豊田市指定有形民俗文化財。[[1973]]（[[昭和]]48年）[[2月15日]]指定。六所神社管理。[[1872]]（明治5年）に六所神社下宮の[[境内]]に建てられた木造平屋[[茅葺]]の舞台で、間口は8[[間]]（14.5メートル）、奥行きは4.7間（8.5メートル）[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html 六所神社舞台]（豊田市郷土資料館ウェブページ、2012年[[4月2日]]閲覧）。このうち12.6メートルある舞台間口は一本の太い[[梁 (建築)|梁]]（90センチメートル×60センチメートル）が通しで支えており、屋根は[[合掌材]]の中途に梁を渡すことで支持されている。内部では登場者を乗せて上下する「二重仕掛」と呼ばれるからくりがあり、[[明治時代]]前期の古式をよく伝えているといわれる。木材は六所山で伐採された[[スギ]]・[[ヒノキ]]・[[クリ]]・[[モミ]]などで、材料の運搬には近隣の[[氏子]]が多数参加し、木材が岩角に突き当たった時には岩角を削って搬出したとされる現地案内板より。。そして[[棟上げ]]には早朝から多数の見物人が集まり、大変なにぎわいであったという『松平町誌』：812ページ。 舞台の東隣に立っている[[クスノキ]]と[[イチョウ]]は、[[大正天皇]]の[[即位]]記念として植樹されたものである『松平町誌』：323ページ。 === 古六所（ころくしょ）神社 === 所在地は坂上町字古社（旧松平町㮛立（そだめ））（{{ウィキ座標|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|座標}}）。神明社末社の小石祠。[[妙昌寺 (豊田市)|大簗山妙昌寺]]古記集によれば、簗山（現[[王滝町]]）にある妙昌寺3世[[住職]]無染融了（むぜんゆうりょう）上人が[[シキミ]]の採取のために山に入ったところ、[[笈]]を松の木にかけて休息している老人と出会った。無染上人が誰何したところ、自分は奥州鹽竈明神である、と老人は応え、この近隣に住まう氏子の守護のために出張してきたので定住先を選ぶように、と言い残して煙のように消えてしまった。驚いた無染上人はこの話を松平親氏に伝え、松平親氏はまずこの地に奥州鹽竈明神を勧請した後に、蜂ケ峰に[[地蔵尊]]6体を勧請して六所大明神としたという『松平町誌』：779-780ページ。 Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|古六所神社

［下宮］流造[[板葺]] |別名= |札所等= |例祭=[[9月23日]] |神事= }} '''六所神社'''（ろくしょじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[豊田市]][[坂上町 (豊田市)|坂上町]]にある[[神社]]である。旧[[社格]]は[[県社]]。 == Overview == 上宮・八ケ峰神社・下宮などで構成される神社の総称でもある。[[祭神]]は[[サルタヒコ|猿田毘古神]]（サルタヒコ）・[[シオツチノオジ|塩椎神]]（シオツチノオジ）・[[岐の神]]・[[ヤマトタケル|日本武尊]]（やまとたけるのみこと）。[[流造]][[銅板葺]]の[[本殿]]、旧篭屋を転用した[[覆殿]]（以上上宮）、流造[[板葺]]の假本殿、[[木構造 (建築)|木造]]銅板葺の覆殿、木造[[平屋]][[瓦葺]]の[[祭文殿]]・[[渡殿]]・[[拝殿]]・[[神楽殿]]、[[舞台]]（豊田市指定有形民俗文化財）、流造木造平屋瓦葺の[[社務所]]、[[神庫]]、流造銅板葺の[[秋葉神社]]本殿（以上下宮）、流造[[桧皮葺]]の本殿（以上八ケ峰神社）、一の[[鳥居]]、二の鳥居、三の鳥居などで構成される『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ。上宮は[[六所山]]の山頂にほど近い山麓に鎮座し、八ケ峰神社は上宮よりわずかに北にあり、下宮の所在地は坂上町字地蔵堂、一の鳥居の所在地は坂上町字金姓などとなる。 Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|六所神社一の鳥居。奥手に望むのは六所山。

（2012年（平成24年）4月） == 歴史 == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|六所山遠景
（豊田市坂上町、2019年（令和元年）11月）]] 六所山は古来より[[猿投山]]・[[本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|本宮山]]と共に[[三河国]]三霊山のひとつとされ、山自体が[[神体]]とされて[[大山積神]]（オオヤマツミ）など6柱の祭神が奉祀されていた『松平町誌』：758-759ページ。現在でも字金姓の小台地にたたずむ一の鳥居は、六所山を遙拝するのに最も適した場所にあり、古代、この地に最初期の遙拝所が建てられたものとも推察し得る『坂上町誌』：10ページ。後に[[社殿]]の築造という[[仏教]]文化に由来する概念が国内に浸透し、六所山山頂にも社殿が築かれることになるのは遅くとも[[平安時代]]末期頃と考えられており、上宮近辺で平安時代から[[室町時代]]にかけての[[土器]]（かわらけ）片が発見されるのは、この地でこの時代に[[祭祀]]が行われていたことを裏付けるものである『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ。なお、[[1604]]（[[慶長]]9年）の『慶長検地帳』には鳥居下という地名がみられることから一の鳥居がこの時期にすでに築造されていたと推定されるが、建立そのものの時期はよく分かっていない。鳥居の両際には長らくマツの巨木が立ちそびえており、2本とも[[樹齢]]500年以上と言われていたが、[[1959]]（[[昭和]]34年）[[9月]]に上陸した[[伊勢湾台風]]によって倒れている『坂上町誌』：88ページ。 一帯はかつては[[松平郷]]といい、[[松平氏]]（[[徳川氏]]）発祥の地である。[[1377]]（[[永和 (日本)|永和]]3年・[[天授 (日本)|天授]]3年）[[8月19日 (旧暦)|8月19日]]、松平宗家初代[[松平親氏|松平太郎左衛門親氏]]が[[Mutsu Province |奥州]]より鹽竈（しおがま）六所明神（[[鹽竈神社]]の六所宮の神）を六所山に勧請した上で奉祀したとされる。それまで「吉木山」「蜂ケ峰山」などとされていた山名が、以降六所山と呼ばれるようになる。[[産土神]]として奉拝されていた[[大山祇神]]はその社地を譲って北東の蜂ケ峰に遷され、以来「隠居神様」と呼ばれながら六所神社[[摂社]]の八ケ峰神社として存続することになる一方、新たに祀られた[[客人神]]の本殿は芳樹宮と名付けられ、六所大明神と称されて、松平氏・徳川氏の[[氏神]]として歴代当主の崇拝を受けていくことになる『松平町誌』：759ページ。早くも[[1474]]（[[応仁]]元年）には松平宗家第4代[[松平親忠]]が、[[1520]]（[[永正]]元年）には松平宗家第5代[[松平長親]]が社殿の再建に取り組んでいる。[[1527]]（[[大永]]7年）12月には野火で社殿が全焼したが、このとき松平長親と松平宗家第6代[[松平信忠]]は連署の上、松平家一門に対して殿舎再建への[[寄進]]を依頼している。なお、下宮は六所山南麓にある槙ケ田和村（現豊田市[[花沢町]]）に鎮座していたのを現在地に移し、当地を宮口村と名付けて社領としたのも松平長親だとする伝承が残っている『坂上町誌』：245ページ。[[1542]]（[[天文 (元号)|天文]]11年）に松平宗家第8代[[松平広忠]]に[[嫡子]]竹千代が誕生した際に礼拝がなされたといわれる高宮村（現[[岡崎市]][[明大寺町]]）の[[六所神社 (岡崎市)|六所神社]]に対し、竹千代長じて[[岡崎城]]城主となった[[徳川家康]]は、[[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku]]年間（[[1558]] - [[1570]]）に六所山六所大明神の祭神6柱のうち3柱を勧請し、遷座したという『坂上町誌』：246ページ。ただし岡崎市誌によれば、松平広忠寄進状などの史料より[[1546]]（天文15年）以前にはすでに遷座していたことがうかがわれる『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ。 {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikauji, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|松平親氏像
（豊田市[[松平町 (豊田市)|松平町]]、2019年（令和元年）8月） Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|徳川家康像
（[[狩野探幽]]画、[[大阪城]]天守閣蔵） }} [[1590]]（[[天正]]18年）の徳川家康[[関東]]移封の後は岡崎城城主[[田中吉政]]の支配下に入り、[[寺社領]]の没収を受けるが、[[1602]]（慶長7年）に徳川家康より高20石の大明神初穂料を下賜される。[[江戸時代]]に入ると、[[1617]]（[[元和 (日本)|元和]]3年）には[[松平太郎左衛門家]]第8代[[松平由重]]によって本殿が造営されるのと同時に[[玄米]]4石7斗8升3合が例祭料・灯明料として宮口村高より免引され『松平町誌』：760ページ、[[1638]]（[[寛永]]15年）には松平太郎左衛門家第10代[[松平重和]]によって再び本殿が造営され、[[1667]]（[[寛文]]7年）・[[1683]]（[[天和 (日本)|天和]]3年）・[[1686]]（[[貞享]]4年）には[[奥殿藩]][[大給松平家]]初代[[松平乗次]]によって堂宇が再建・改修され、[[1736]]（[[元文]]元年）から翌年にかけては奥殿藩大給松平家第4代[[松平盈乗]]による堂宇の再建、灯明料として玄米2石4斗の寄進、例祭料として7斗8升3合の免引などがあり、[[1779]]（[[安永 (元号)|安永]]8年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第5代[[松平乗穏]]による堂宇の造営『松平町誌』：761ページ、[[1790]]（[[寛政]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第7代[[松平乗尹]]による堂宇の造営、奥殿藩大給松平家第7代[[松平乗尹]]による堂宇の造営、[[1849]]（[[嘉永]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第9代[[松平乗利]]による下宮における[[不動一宇]]の造営、[[1858]]（[[安政]]5年）と[[1861]]（[[文久]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第10代松平乗謨及び松平太郎左衛門家第16代[[松平頼載]]によって本殿の再興・修復、鳥居の再興が行われるなど、徳川家・松平家一門、とりわけ宮口村領主である大給松平家と松平郷を領した松平太郎左衛門家による厚遇ぶりには枚挙の暇がない。 [[1873]]（[[明治]]6年）、六所大明神から'''六所神社'''と改称する。旧社格は[[郷社]]で、[[1917]]（[[大正]]6年）には御料林となっていた六所山社有林の払い下げが許可され、翌[[1918]]（大正7年）から[[1920]]（大正9年）にかけて下宮の拝殿及び祭文殿が再建、[[1921]]（大正10年）には県社に昇格している。現在は愛知県[[神社庁]]に属し、[[登記]]名を[[宗教法人]]六所神社としている『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ。 == 主な祭典行事 == * [[1月1日]]：[[歳旦祭]] * [[2月11日]]：紀元祭 * [[2月17日]]：[[祈年祭]]、秋葉神社祭、山の神祭 * [[6月30日]]：[[大祓]] * [[7月25日]]：八ヶ峰神社祭 * [[9月1日]]：二百十日祭、熱田祭 * [[9月22日]]：神迎え神事・前日祭 * [[9月23日]]：[[例祭]]・神送り神事 * [[11月23日]]：[[新嘗祭]] * [[12月31日]]：大祓・除夜祭 * 毎月1日：[[月次祭]] == 境内社 == * 八ヶ峰神社（上宮）：大山祇神（通称：「隠居神様」） * 秋葉神社（下宮）：軻遇突智神 == その他 == === 六所神社の舞台 === [[File:Rokusho Jinja Stage 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|六所神社舞台
（2019年（令和元年）11月）]] 豊田市指定有形民俗文化財。[[1973]]（[[昭和]]48年）[[2月15日]]指定。六所神社管理。[[1872]]（明治5年）に六所神社下宮の[[境内]]に建てられた木造平屋[[茅葺]]の舞台で、間口は8[[間]]（14.5メートル）、奥行きは4.7間（8.5メートル）[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html 六所神社舞台]（豊田市郷土資料館ウェブページ、2012年[[4月2日]]閲覧）。このうち12.6メートルある舞台間口は一本の太い[[梁 (建築)|梁]]（90センチメートル×60センチメートル）が通しで支えており、屋根は[[合掌材]]の中途に梁を渡すことで支持されている。内部では登場者を乗せて上下する「二重仕掛」と呼ばれるからくりがあり、[[明治時代]]前期の古式をよく伝えているといわれる。木材は六所山で伐採された[[スギ]]・[[ヒノキ]]・[[クリ]]・[[モミ]]などで、材料の運搬には近隣の[[氏子]]が多数参加し、木材が岩角に突き当たった時には岩角を削って搬出したとされる現地案内板より。。そして[[棟上げ]]には早朝から多数の見物人が集まり、大変なにぎわいであったという『松平町誌』：812ページ。 舞台の東隣に立っている[[クスノキ]]と[[イチョウ]]は、[[大正天皇]]の[[即位]]記念として植樹されたものである『松平町誌』：323ページ。 === 古六所（ころくしょ）神社 === 所在地は坂上町字古社（旧松平町㮛立（そだめ））（{{ウィキ座標|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|座標}}）。神明社末社の小石祠。[[妙昌寺 (豊田市)|大簗山妙昌寺]]古記集によれば、簗山（現[[王滝町]]）にある妙昌寺3世[[住職]]無染融了（むぜんゆうりょう）上人が[[シキミ]]の採取のために山に入ったところ、[[笈]]を松の木にかけて休息している老人と出会った。無染上人が誰何したところ、自分は奥州鹽竈明神である、と老人は応え、この近隣に住まう氏子の守護のために出張してきたので定住先を選ぶように、と言い残して煙のように消えてしまった。驚いた無染上人はこの話を松平親氏に伝え、松平親氏はまずこの地に奥州鹽竈明神を勧請した後に、蜂ケ峰に[[地蔵尊]]6体を勧請して六所大明神としたという『松平町誌』：779-780ページ。 Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|古六所神社

［下宮］流造[[板葺]] |別名= |札所等= |例祭=[[9月23日]] |神事= }} '''六所神社'''（ろくしょじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[豊田市]][[坂上町 (豊田市)|坂上町]]にある[[神社]]である。旧[[社格]]は[[県社]]。 == Overview == 上宮・八ケ峰神社・下宮などで構成される神社の総称でもある。[[祭神]]は[[サルタヒコ|猿田毘古神]]（サルタヒコ）・[[シオツチノオジ|塩椎神]]（シオツチノオジ）・[[岐の神]]・[[ヤマトタケル|日本武尊]]（やまとたけるのみこと）。[[流造]][[銅板葺]]の[[本殿]]、旧篭屋を転用した[[覆殿]]（以上上宮）、流造[[板葺]]の假本殿、[[木構造 (建築)|木造]]銅板葺の覆殿、木造[[平屋]][[瓦葺]]の[[祭文殿]]・[[渡殿]]・[[拝殿]]・[[神楽殿]]、[[舞台]]（豊田市指定有形民俗文化財）、流造木造平屋瓦葺の[[社務所]]、[[神庫]]、流造銅板葺の[[秋葉神社]]本殿（以上下宮）、流造[[桧皮葺]]の本殿（以上八ケ峰神社）、一の[[鳥居]]、二の鳥居、三の鳥居などで構成される『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ。上宮は[[六所山]]の山頂にほど近い山麓に鎮座し、八ケ峰神社は上宮よりわずかに北にあり、下宮の所在地は坂上町字地蔵堂、一の鳥居の所在地は坂上町字金姓などとなる。 Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|六所神社一の鳥居。奥手に望むのは六所山。

（豊田市坂上町、2019年（令和元年）11月）]] 六所山は古来より[[猿投山]]・[[本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|本宮山]]と共に[[三河国]]三霊山のひとつとされ、山自体が[[神体]]とされて[[大山積神]]（オオヤマツミ）など6柱の祭神が奉祀されていた『松平町誌』：758-759ページ。現在でも字金姓の小台地にたたずむ一の鳥居は、六所山を遙拝するのに最も適した場所にあり、古代、この地に最初期の遙拝所が建てられたものとも推察し得る『坂上町誌』：10ページ。後に[[社殿]]の築造という[[仏教]]文化に由来する概念が国内に浸透し、六所山山頂にも社殿が築かれることになるのは遅くとも[[平安時代]]末期頃と考えられており、上宮近辺で平安時代から[[室町時代]]にかけての[[土器]]（かわらけ）片が発見されるのは、この地でこの時代に[[祭祀]]が行われていたことを裏付けるものである『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ。なお、[[1604]]（[[慶長]]9年）の『慶長検地帳』には鳥居下という地名がみられることから一の鳥居がこの時期にすでに築造されていたと推定されるが、建立そのものの時期はよく分かっていない。鳥居の両際には長らくマツの巨木が立ちそびえており、2本とも[[樹齢]]500年以上と言われていたが、[[1959]]（[[昭和]]34年）[[9月]]に上陸した[[伊勢湾台風]]によって倒れている『坂上町誌』：88ページ。 一帯はかつては[[松平郷]]といい、[[松平氏]]（[[徳川氏]]）発祥の地である。[[1377]]（[[永和 (日本)|永和]]3年・[[天授 (日本)|天授]]3年）[[8月19日 (旧暦)|8月19日]]、松平宗家初代[[松平親氏|松平太郎左衛門親氏]]が[[Mutsu Province |奥州]]より鹽竈（しおがま）六所明神（[[鹽竈神社]]の六所宮の神）を六所山に勧請した上で奉祀したとされる。それまで「吉木山」「蜂ケ峰山」などとされていた山名が、以降六所山と呼ばれるようになる。[[産土神]]として奉拝されていた[[大山祇神]]はその社地を譲って北東の蜂ケ峰に遷され、以来「隠居神様」と呼ばれながら六所神社[[摂社]]の八ケ峰神社として存続することになる一方、新たに祀られた[[客人神]]の本殿は芳樹宮と名付けられ、六所大明神と称されて、松平氏・徳川氏の[[氏神]]として歴代当主の崇拝を受けていくことになる『松平町誌』：759ページ。早くも[[1474]]（[[応仁]]元年）には松平宗家第4代[[松平親忠]]が、[[1520]]（[[永正]]元年）には松平宗家第5代[[松平長親]]が社殿の再建に取り組んでいる。[[1527]]（[[大永]]7年）12月には野火で社殿が全焼したが、このとき松平長親と松平宗家第6代[[松平信忠]]は連署の上、松平家一門に対して殿舎再建への[[寄進]]を依頼している。なお、下宮は六所山南麓にある槙ケ田和村（現豊田市[[花沢町]]）に鎮座していたのを現在地に移し、当地を宮口村と名付けて社領としたのも松平長親だとする伝承が残っている『坂上町誌』：245ページ。[[1542]]（[[天文 (元号)|天文]]11年）に松平宗家第8代[[松平広忠]]に[[嫡子]]竹千代が誕生した際に礼拝がなされたといわれる高宮村（現[[岡崎市]][[明大寺町]]）の[[六所神社 (岡崎市)|六所神社]]に対し、竹千代長じて[[岡崎城]]城主となった[[徳川家康]]は、[[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku]]年間（[[1558]] - [[1570]]）に六所山六所大明神の祭神6柱のうち3柱を勧請し、遷座したという『坂上町誌』：246ページ。ただし岡崎市誌によれば、松平広忠寄進状などの史料より[[1546]]（天文15年）以前にはすでに遷座していたことがうかがわれる『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ。 {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikauji, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|松平親氏像
（豊田市[[松平町 (豊田市)|松平町]]、2019年（令和元年）8月） Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|徳川家康像
（[[狩野探幽]]画、[[大阪城]]天守閣蔵） }} [[1590]]（[[天正]]18年）の徳川家康[[関東]]移封の後は岡崎城城主[[田中吉政]]の支配下に入り、[[寺社領]]の没収を受けるが、[[1602]]（慶長7年）に徳川家康より高20石の大明神初穂料を下賜される。[[江戸時代]]に入ると、[[1617]]（[[元和 (日本)|元和]]3年）には[[松平太郎左衛門家]]第8代[[松平由重]]によって本殿が造営されるのと同時に[[玄米]]4石7斗8升3合が例祭料・灯明料として宮口村高より免引され『松平町誌』：760ページ、[[1638]]（[[寛永]]15年）には松平太郎左衛門家第10代[[松平重和]]によって再び本殿が造営され、[[1667]]（[[寛文]]7年）・[[1683]]（[[天和 (日本)|天和]]3年）・[[1686]]（[[貞享]]4年）には[[奥殿藩]][[大給松平家]]初代[[松平乗次]]によって堂宇が再建・改修され、[[1736]]（[[元文]]元年）から翌年にかけては奥殿藩大給松平家第4代[[松平盈乗]]による堂宇の再建、灯明料として玄米2石4斗の寄進、例祭料として7斗8升3合の免引などがあり、[[1779]]（[[安永 (元号)|安永]]8年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第5代[[松平乗穏]]による堂宇の造営『松平町誌』：761ページ、[[1790]]（[[寛政]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第7代[[松平乗尹]]による堂宇の造営、奥殿藩大給松平家第7代[[松平乗尹]]による堂宇の造営、[[1849]]（[[嘉永]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第9代[[松平乗利]]による下宮における[[不動一宇]]の造営、[[1858]]（[[安政]]5年）と[[1861]]（[[文久]]2年）には奥殿藩大給松平家第10代松平乗謨及び松平太郎左衛門家第16代[[松平頼載]]によって本殿の再興・修復、鳥居の再興が行われるなど、徳川家・松平家一門、とりわけ宮口村領主である大給松平家と松平郷を領した松平太郎左衛門家による厚遇ぶりには枚挙の暇がない。 [[1873]]（[[明治]]6年）、六所大明神から'''六所神社'''と改称する。旧社格は[[郷社]]で、[[1917]]（[[大正]]6年）には御料林となっていた六所山社有林の払い下げが許可され、翌[[1918]]（大正7年）から[[1920]]（大正9年）にかけて下宮の拝殿及び祭文殿が再建、[[1921]]（大正10年）には県社に昇格している。現在は愛知県[[神社庁]]に属し、[[登記]]名を[[宗教法人]]六所神社としている『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ。 == 主な祭典行事 == * [[1月1日]]：[[歳旦祭]] * [[2月11日]]：紀元祭 * [[2月17日]]：[[祈年祭]]、秋葉神社祭、山の神祭 * [[6月30日]]：[[大祓]] * [[7月25日]]：八ヶ峰神社祭 * [[9月1日]]：二百十日祭、熱田祭 * [[9月22日]]：神迎え神事・前日祭 * [[9月23日]]：[[例祭]]・神送り神事 * [[11月23日]]：[[新嘗祭]] * [[12月31日]]：大祓・除夜祭 * 毎月1日：[[月次祭]] == 境内社 == * 八ヶ峰神社（上宮）：大山祇神（通称：「隠居神様」） * 秋葉神社（下宮）：軻遇突智神 == その他 == === 六所神社の舞台 === [[File:Rokusho Jinja Stage 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|六所神社舞台
（2019年（令和元年）11月）]] 豊田市指定有形民俗文化財。[[1973]]（[[昭和]]48年）[[2月15日]]指定。六所神社管理。[[1872]]（明治5年）に六所神社下宮の[[境内]]に建てられた木造平屋[[茅葺]]の舞台で、間口は8[[間]]（14.5メートル）、奥行きは4.7間（8.5メートル）[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html 六所神社舞台]（豊田市郷土資料館ウェブページ、2012年[[4月2日]]閲覧）。このうち12.6メートルある舞台間口は一本の太い[[梁 (建築)|梁]]（90センチメートル×60センチメートル）が通しで支えており、屋根は[[合掌材]]の中途に梁を渡すことで支持されている。内部では登場者を乗せて上下する「二重仕掛」と呼ばれるからくりがあり、[[明治時代]]前期の古式をよく伝えているといわれる。木材は六所山で伐採された[[スギ]]・[[ヒノキ]]・[[クリ]]・[[モミ]]などで、材料の運搬には近隣の[[氏子]]が多数参加し、木材が岩角に突き当たった時には岩角を削って搬出したとされる現地案内板より。。そして[[棟上げ]]には早朝から多数の見物人が集まり、大変なにぎわいであったという『松平町誌』：812ページ。 舞台の東隣に立っている[[クスノキ]]と[[イチョウ]]は、[[大正天皇]]の[[即位]]記念として植樹されたものである『松平町誌』：323ページ。 === 古六所（ころくしょ）神社 === 所在地は坂上町字古社（旧松平町㮛立（そだめ））（{{ウィキ座標|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|座標}}）。神明社末社の小石祠。[[妙昌寺 (豊田市)|大簗山妙昌寺]]古記集によれば、簗山（現[[王滝町]]）にある妙昌寺3世[[住職]]無染融了（むぜんゆうりょう）上人が[[シキミ]]の採取のために山に入ったところ、[[笈]]を松の木にかけて休息している老人と出会った。無染上人が誰何したところ、自分は奥州鹽竈明神である、と老人は応え、この近隣に住まう氏子の守護のために出張してきたので定住先を選ぶように、と言い残して煙のように消えてしまった。驚いた無染上人はこの話を松平親氏に伝え、松平親氏はまずこの地に奥州鹽竈明神を勧請した後に、蜂ケ峰に[[地蔵尊]]6体を勧請して六所大明神としたという『松平町誌』：779-780ページ。 Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|古六所神社

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. (2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) March) Myoushou-ji, Outaki-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Ōyanayama Myōchōji
(Toyota City, Ōtaki Town, 2012 (Heisei 24) May) == References == {{Footnote Help}} == Sources == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Matsudaira Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “{{ill|Matsudaira Town Chronicle|ja|松平町 (豊田市)|lt=Matsudaira Town Chronicle|lt_ja=松平町誌}}”, Toyota City Board of Education, {{ill|1976|ja|1976}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 51). * Sakaue Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “Sakaue Town Chronicle”, Sakaue Town, {{ill|1991|ja|1991}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 3). * Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary Compilation Committee, “Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary 23: Aichi Prefecture”, Kadokawa Shoten, {{ill|1989|ja|1989}} (Heisei 1). {{Shinto Yok}} [[Category:Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Toyota City]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties of Municipalities]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyota City]] [[Category:Yamato Takeru]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:completion tier 1]][[ja:六所神社]]

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|First Torii of Rokusho Shrine. In the background stands Rokusho Mountain.
({{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year) November) Rokusho Jinja Jouku 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.jpg|Upper Shrine of Rokusho Shrine

(2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) March) Myoushou-ji, Outaki-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Ōyanayama Myōchōji
(Toyota City, Ōtaki Town, 2012 (Heisei 24) May) == References == {{Footnote Help}} == Sources == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Matsudaira Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “{{ill|Matsudaira Town Chronicle|ja|松平町 (豊田市)|lt=Matsudaira Town Chronicle|lt_ja=松平町誌}}”, Toyota City Board of Education, {{ill|1976|ja|1976}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 51). * Sakaue Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “Sakaue Town Chronicle”, Sakaue Town, {{ill|1991|ja|1991}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 3). * Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary Compilation Committee, “Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary 23: Aichi Prefecture”, Kadokawa Shoten, {{ill|1989|ja|1989}} (Heisei 1). {{Shinto Yok}} [[Category:Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Toyota City]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties of Municipalities]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyota City]] [[Category:Yamato Takeru]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Toyota)]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:六所神社]]

{{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} |Rank = Prefectural Shrine |Founded = {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3) |Main Hall = [Upper Shrine] {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}
[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|First Torii of Rokusho Shrine. In the background stands Rokusho Mountain.
({{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year) November) Rokusho Jinja Jouku 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.jpg|Upper Shrine of Rokusho Shrine
({{ill|2012|ja|2012}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 24) April) Hachigamine Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Hachigamine Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) April) Rokusho Jinja Geku Haiden, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Lower Shrine Worship Hall of Rokusho Shrine
(2019 (Reiwa first year) November) Jinguji Ato, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Site of Jinguji Hoshoji
(2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. (2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue

In {{ill|1849|ja|1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town.
