(2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) March) Myoushou-ji, Outaki-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Ōyanayama Myōchōji
(Toyota City, Ōtaki Town, 2012 (Heisei 24) May) == References == {{Footnote Help}} == Sources == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Matsudaira Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “{{ill|Matsudaira Town Chronicle|ja|松平町 (豊田市)|lt=Matsudaira Town Chronicle|lt_ja=松平町誌}}”, Toyota City Board of Education, {{ill|1976|ja|1976}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 51). * Sakaue Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “Sakaue Town Chronicle”, Sakaue Town, {{ill|1991|ja|1991}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 3). * Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary Compilation Committee, “Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary 23: Aichi Prefecture”, Kadokawa Shoten, {{ill|1989|ja|1989}} (Heisei 1). {{Shinto Yok}} [[Category:Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Toyota City]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties of Municipalities]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyota City]] [[Category:Yamato Takeru]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Toyota)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Toyota)]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:六所神社]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:New]]

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神|1=Kunado-no-Kami}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|First Torii of Rokusho Shrine. In the background stands Rokusho Mountain.

(2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain

On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) March) Myoushou-ji, Outaki-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Ōyanayama Myōchōji
(Toyota City, Ōtaki Town, 2012 (Heisei 24) May) == References == {{Footnote Help}} == Sources == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Matsudaira Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “{{ill|Matsudaira Town Chronicle|ja|松平町 (豊田市)|lt=Matsudaira Town Chronicle|lt_ja=松平町誌}}”, Toyota City Board of Education, {{ill|1976|ja|1976}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 51). * Sakaue Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “Sakaue Town Chronicle”, Sakaue Town, {{ill|1991|ja|1991}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 3). * Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary Compilation Committee, “Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary 23: Aichi Prefecture”, Kadokawa Shoten, {{ill|1989|ja|1989}} (Heisei 1). {{Shinto Yok}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Toyota City]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties of Municipalities]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyota City]] [[Category:Yamato Takeru]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Toyota)]] [[ja:六所神社]]

({{ill|2019|ja|2019|12=draft}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和|12=draft}} first year) November) |Location = [Upper Shrine] Aichi Prefecture Toyota City Sakaue-cho, 1 Rokusho Mountain

{{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神|1=Kunado-no-Kami|12=draft}}
{{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊|12=draft}} |Rank = Prefectural Shrine |Founded = {{ill|1377|ja|1377|12=draft}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授|12=draft}} 3) |Main Hall = [Upper Shrine] {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|12=draft}} {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=draft}}
[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=draft}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日|12=draft}} |Rituals = }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|ja|愛知県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Toyota City|ja|豊田市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町|12=draft}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=draft}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神|12=draft}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神|12=draft}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神|12=draft}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神|1=Kunado-no-Kami|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊|12=draft}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|12=draft}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=draft}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=draft}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺|12=draft}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿|12=draft}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿|12=draft}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿|12=draft}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台|12=draft}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所|12=draft}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫|12=draft}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=draft}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=draft}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺|12=draft}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居|12=draft}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=draft}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|First Torii of Rokusho Shrine. In the background stands Rokusho Mountain.
({{ill|2019|ja|2019|12=draft}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和|12=draft}} first year) November) Rokusho Jinja Jouku 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.jpg|Upper Shrine of Rokusho Shrine
({{ill|2012|ja|2012|12=draft}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|12=draft}} 24) April) Hachigamine Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Hachigamine Shrine

(2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019|12=draft}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和|12=draft}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=draft}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山|12=draft}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国|12=draft}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体|12=draft}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神|12=draft}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿|12=draft}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教|12=draft}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器|12=draft}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀|12=draft}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風|12=draft}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月|12=draft}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷|12=draft}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏|12=draft}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏|12=draft}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日|12=draft}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377|12=draft}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授|12=draft}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏|12=draft}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社|12=draft}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州|12=draft}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神|12=draft}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=draft}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社|12=draft}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神|12=draft}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神|12=draft}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474|12=draft}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁|12=draft}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠|12=draft}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520|12=draft}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正|12=draft}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親|12=draft}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527|12=draft}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永|12=draft}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠|12=draft}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進|12=draft}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町|12=draft}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542|12=draft}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文|12=draft}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠|12=draft}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子|12=draft}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市|12=draft}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町|12=draft}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城|12=draft}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku|12=draft}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558|12=draft}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570|12=draft}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546|12=draft}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和|12=draft}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽|12=draft}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=draft}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590|12=draft}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|12=draft}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康|12=draft}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東|12=draft}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政|12=draft}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602|12=draft}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617|12=draft}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和|12=draft}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重|12=draft}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米|12=draft}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|12=draft}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和|12=draft}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683|12=draft}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和|12=draft}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686|12=draft}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享|12=draft}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家|12=draft}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次|12=draft}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736|12=draft}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文|12=draft}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗|12=draft}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779|12=draft}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永|12=draft}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏|12=draft}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政|12=draft}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹|12=draft}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永|12=draft}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇|12=draft}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利|12=draft}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858|12=draft}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|12=draft}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861|12=draft}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久|12=draft}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨|12=draft}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載|12=draft}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917|12=draft}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正|12=draft}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918|12=draft}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920|12=draft}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921|12=draft}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁|12=draft}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=draft}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|12=draft}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日|12=draft}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓|12=draft}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日|12=draft}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日|12=draft}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日|12=draft}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭|12=draft}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|12=draft}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=draft}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=draft}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神|12=draft}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872|12=draft}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間|12=draft}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁|12=draft}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材|12=draft}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ|12=draft}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ|12=draft}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ|12=draft}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子|12=draft}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ|12=draft}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺|12=draft}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot|12=draft}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ|12=draft}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈|12=draft}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神|12=draft}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine

Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=draft}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神|12=draft}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田毘古神|12=draft}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神|12=draft}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Gino-no-Kami|ja|岐の神|1=Kunado-no-Kami|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊|12=draft}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|12=draft}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=draft}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=draft}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺|12=draft}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿|12=draft}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿|12=draft}}, {{ill|Worship Hall|ja|拝殿|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Kagura Hall|ja|神楽殿|12=draft}}; a {{ill|Stage|ja|舞台|12=draft}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所|12=draft}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫|12=draft}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=draft}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=draft}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺|12=draft}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居|12=draft}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=draft}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. (2012 (Heisei 24) April) == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|ja|2019|12=draft}} ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和|12=draft}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=draft}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hongu Mountain|ja|本宮山 (岡崎市・豊川市・新城市)|lt=Hongu Mountain|lt_ja=本宮山|12=draft}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|ja|三河国|12=draft}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体|1=Shintai|12=draft}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神|12=draft}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿|12=draft}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|ja|仏教|12=draft}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|12=draft}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器|12=draft}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀|12=draft}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風|12=draft}} that struck in {{ill|September|ja|9月|12=draft}} {{ill|1959|ja|1959|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷|12=draft}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|ja|松平氏|12=draft}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|ja|徳川氏|12=draft}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|ja|8月19日|12=draft}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|ja|1377|12=draft}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=draft}} 3, {{ill|Tenju|ja|天授|12=draft}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikaue|ja|松平親氏|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue|lt_ja=松平太郎左衛門親氏|12=draft}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama Shrine|ja|鹽竈神社|12=draft}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|lt=Ōshū|lt_ja=奥州|12=draft}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|産土神|12=draft}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=draft}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂社|12=draft}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神|12=draft}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|ja|氏神|12=draft}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|ja|1474|12=draft}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin era|ja|応仁|12=draft}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠|12=draft}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|ja|1520|12=draft}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō era|ja|永正|12=draft}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親|12=draft}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|ja|1527|12=draft}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei era|ja|大永|12=draft}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|ja|松平信忠|12=draft}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進|12=draft}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町|12=draft}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|ja|1542|12=draft}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenmon era|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenmon|lt_ja=天文|12=draft}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|ja|松平広忠|12=draft}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子|12=draft}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki City|ja|岡崎市|12=draft}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町|12=draft}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|ja|岡崎城|12=draft}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku|12=draft}} ({{ill|1558|ja|1558|12=draft}}–{{ill|1570|ja|1570|12=draft}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|ja|1546|12=draft}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze Statue of Matsudaira Chikaue, Matsudaira-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa|ja|令和|12=draft}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kano Tanyu|ja|狩野探幽|12=draft}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=draft}}) }} After {{ill|1590|ja|1590|12=draft}} ({{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|12=draft}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|徳川家康|12=draft}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東|12=draft}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政|12=draft}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|ja|1602|12=draft}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, in {{ill|1617|ja|1617|12=draft}} ({{ill|Genwa|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genwa|lt_ja=元和|12=draft}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重|12=draft}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown Rice|ja|玄米|12=draft}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|ja|1638|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|12=draft}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和|12=draft}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|ja|1667|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kanbun|ja|寛文|12=draft}} 7), {{ill|1683|ja|1683|12=draft}} ({{ill|Tennai|ja|天和 (日本)|lt=Tennai|lt_ja=天和|12=draft}} 3), and {{ill|1686|ja|1686|12=draft}} ({{ill|Jokyō|ja|貞享|12=draft}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okudono-han|ja|奥殿藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家|12=draft}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次|12=draft}}. From {{ill|1736|ja|1736|12=draft}} ({{ill|Genbun|ja|元文|12=draft}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗|12=draft}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|ja|1779|12=draft}} ({{ill|An'ei|ja|安永 (元号)|lt=An'ei|lt_ja=安永|12=draft}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏|12=draft}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|ja|1790|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政|12=draft}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹|12=draft}}. In {{ill|1849|ja|1849|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永|12=draft}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇|12=draft}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利|12=draft}}. In {{ill|1858|ja|1858|12=draft}} ({{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|12=draft}} 5) and {{ill|1861|ja|1861|12=draft}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|ja|文久|12=draft}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨|12=draft}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載|12=draft}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|ja|1873|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, and in {{ill|1917|ja|1917|12=draft}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正|12=draft}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|ja|1918|12=draft}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|ja|1920|12=draft}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921|ja|1921|12=draft}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁|12=draft}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=draft}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|12=draft}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭|12=draft}} * {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日|12=draft}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|ja|2月17日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Harvest Festival|ja|祈年祭|12=draft}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Great Purification|ja|大祓|12=draft}} * {{ill|July 25|ja|7月25日|12=draft}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日|12=draft}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|ja|9月22日|12=draft}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|ja|9月23日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭|12=draft}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|ja|11月23日|12=draft}}: {{ill|Niiname-sai|ja|新嘗祭|12=draft}} * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|12=draft}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=draft}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=draft}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=draft}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神|12=draft}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|ja|2月15日|12=draft}}, {{ill|1973|ja|1973|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|ja|1872|12=draft}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|ken|ja|間|12=draft}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁|12=draft}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材|12=draft}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Japanese Cedar|ja|スギ|12=draft}}), cypress ({{ill|Cypress|ja|ヒノキ|12=draft}}), chestnut ({{ill|Chestnut|ja|クリ|12=draft}}), and fir ({{ill|Fir|ja|モミ|12=draft}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子|12=draft}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ|12=draft}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺|12=draft}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot Muzen Yūrō|ja|住職|lt=Legitimate Abbot|12=draft}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Shikimi|ja|シキミ|12=draft}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈|12=draft}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神|12=draft}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) March) Myoushou-ji, Outaki-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Ōyanayama Myōchōji
(Toyota City, Ōtaki Town, 2012 (Heisei 24) May) == References == {{Footnote Help}} == Sources == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Matsudaira Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “{{ill|Matsudaira Town Chronicle|ja|松平町 (豊田市)|lt=Matsudaira Town Chronicle|lt_ja=松平町誌|12=draft}}”, Toyota City Board of Education, {{ill|1976|ja|1976|12=draft}} ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和|12=draft}} 51). * Sakaue Town Chronicle Compilation Committee, “Sakaue Town Chronicle”, Sakaue Town, {{ill|1991|ja|1991|12=draft}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|12=draft}} 3). * Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary Compilation Committee, “Kadokawa Japanese Place Names Dictionary 23: Aichi Prefecture”, Kadokawa Shoten, {{ill|1989|ja|1989|12=draft}} (Heisei 1). {{Shinto Yok}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Toyota City]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Aichi Prefecture]] [[Category:Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties of Municipalities]] [[Category:Buildings in Toyota City]] [[Category:Yamato Takeru]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Toyota)]] [[ja:六所神社]]
