Kami|ja|軻遇突智神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ|1=Kagu-tsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1640658}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on [[:en:February 15|February 15]], [[:en:1973|1973]] ([[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa]] 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 [[:en:Ken (unit)|ken]] (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/beam|1=beam|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11538319}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/thatched roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 明治|1=Meiji period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3125096}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ([[:en:Cryptomeria|Japanese Cedar]]), cypress ([[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Cypress]]), chestnut ([[:en:Castanea crenata|Chestnut]]), and fir ([[:en:Abies firma|Fir]]), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/parishioners|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 氏神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=ujigami|WD=Q767655}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Roof Raising Ceremony|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上棟式|1=raising ceremony|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q106351734}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, [[:en:Abbot (Buddhism)|Legitimate Abbot]] Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of [[:en:Illicium anisatum|Shikimi]], he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/carrying case|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 背負子|1=pack frame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q820964}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine

Its former shrine Rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deities|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}} are [[:en:Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko]] (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シオツチオジ|1=Shiotsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11174872}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), [[:en:Kunado-no-Kami|Kunado-no-Kami]], and [[:en:Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru]] (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|Nagare-zukuri]] style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/copper-sheathed roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tiled roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瓦葺き|1=tiled roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10855730}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Festival Hall|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭文|1=saimon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17991683}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Procession Hall|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Haiden (Shinto)|Worship Hall]], and [[:en:Kagura-den|Kagura Hall]]; a [[:en:Stage (theatre)|Stage]] (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Office|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社|1=Shinto shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q845945}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Treasure House|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cedar-bark roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜皮葺|1=cypress bark roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q90373477}}; and the first, second, and third [[:en:Torii|Torii]], among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. (2012 (Heisei 24) April) [[ja:六所神社 (豊田市)]] == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November [[:en:2019|2019]] ([[:en:Reiwa era|Reiwa]] first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutou Mountain|1=Mount Sanage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11572109}} and [[:en:Mount Hongū (Aichi)|Hongu Mountain]]—as one of the three sacred mountains of [[:en:Mikawa Province|Mikawa Province]]. The mountain itself was revered as a [[:en:Shintai|Shintai]], and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ|1=Ōyamatsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q386563}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|1=Shinto architecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3080012}}—a notion derived from [[:en:Buddhism|Buddhism]]—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]; the discovery of fragments of [[:en:Earthenware|Earthenware]] (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]] in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rituals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭|1=festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q132241}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ([[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the [[:en:Typhoon Vera|Isewan Typhoon]] that struck in [[:en:September|September]] [[:en:1959|1959]] ([[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa]] 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira-go|1=Matsudairagō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11530613}}, the birthplace of the [[:en:Matsudaira clan|Matsudaira clan]] (from which the [[:en:Tokugawa clan|Tokugawa clan]] originated). On [[:en:August 19|August 19]] (old calendar) in [[:en:1377|1377]] ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiwa|1=Eiwa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11131293}} 3, [[:en:Tianshou|Tenju]] 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, [[:en:Matsudaira Chikauji|Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue]], is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of [[:en:Shiogama shrine|Shiogama Shrine]]) from [[:en:Mutsu Province|Ōshū]] onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ([[:en:Ubusunagami|Ubusunagami]]) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|末社|lt=Sessha|1=Setsumatsusha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Subsidiary Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guest Deity|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to まれびと|1=Marebito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6758746}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ([[:en:Ujigami|Ujigami]]) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as [[:en:1474|1474]] (the first year of the [[:en:Ōnin|Ōnin era]]), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Chikatada|1=Matsudaira Chikatada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11239171}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in [[:en:1520|1520]] (the first year of the [[:en:Eishō (Muromachi period)|Eishō era]]) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Nagachika|1=Matsudaira Nagachika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11239108}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December [[:en:1527|1527]] (the 7th year of the [[:en:Daiei (era)|Daiei era]]), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, [[:en:Matsudaira Nobutada|Matsudaira Nobutada]], jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Donation|1=contribution|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11455717}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazawa Town|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In [[:en:1542|1542]] (the 11th year of the [[:en:Tenbun|Tenmon]]), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, [[:en:Matsudaira Hirotada|Matsudaira Hirotada]], had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Legitimate Heir|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 嫡男|1=eldest Di son|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10102290}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day [[:en:Okazaki, Aichi|Okazaki City]] and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meidaiji Town|1=Myōdaijichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17216176}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of [[:en:Okazaki Castle|Okazaki Castle]]—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiroku period|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ([[:en:1558|1558]]–[[:en:1570|1570]]). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to [[:en:1546|1546]].『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze_Statue_of_Matsudaira_Chikauji,_Matsudaira-cho_Toyota_2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ([[:en:Reiwa era|Reiwa]] first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by [[:en:Kanō Tan'yū|Kano Tanyu]], housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Castle|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大坂城}}) }} After [[:en:1590|1590]] ([[:en:Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tenshō Era]] 18) when [[:en:Tokugawa Ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kantō|1=Kantō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11655841}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanaka Yoshimasa|1=Tanaka Yoshimasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11575390}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in [[:en:1602|1602]] ([[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], in [[:en:1617|1617]] ([[:en:Genna|Genwa]] 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|1=Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q115587223}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of [[:en:Brown rice|Brown Rice]] was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In [[:en:1638|1638]] ([[:en:Kan'ei|Kan'ei]] 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Shigekazu|1=Matsudaira Shigefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6829219}}, again built the Main Hall. In [[:en:1667|1667]] ([[:en:Kanbun (era)|Kanbun]] 7), [[:en:1683|1683]] ([[:en:Tenna|Tennai]] 3), and [[:en:1686|1686]] ([[:en:Jōkyō|Jokyō]] 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the [[:en:Okutono Domain|Okudono-han]], {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikyū Matsudaira family|1=Ogyū-Matsudaira clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11260880}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noritsugu|1=Matsudaira Noritsugu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729484}}. From [[:en:1736|1736]] ([[:en:Genbun|Genbun]] 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Eijō|1=Matsudaira Mitsunori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729524}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In [[:en:1779|1779]] ([[:en:An'ei|An'ei]] 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noriomi|1=Matsudaira Noriyasu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729488}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In [[:en:1790|1790]] ([[:en:Kansei|Kansei]] 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Norito|1=Matsudaira Noritada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729477}}. In [[:en:1849|1849]] ([[:en:Kaei|Kaei]] 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fudō Ichiu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noritoshi|1=Matsudaira Noritoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729467}}. In [[:en:1858|1858]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 5) and [[:en:1861|1861]] ([[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noriaki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大給恒|1=Matsudaira Norikata|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6788054}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In [[:en:1873|1873]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and in [[:en:1917|1917]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō]] 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from [[:en:1918|1918]] (Taishō 7) to [[:en:1920|1920]] (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in [[:en:1921 (2021 film)|1921]] (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Agency|1=Jinja-cho|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11590703}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious Corporation|1=religious corporation|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7311343}} Rokusho Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on [[:en:February 15|February 15]], [[:en:1973|1973]] ([[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa]] 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 [[:en:Ken (unit)|ken]] (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/beam|1=beam|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11538319}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/thatched roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 明治|1=Meiji period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3125096}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ([[:en:Cryptomeria|Japanese Cedar]]), cypress ([[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Cypress]]), chestnut ([[:en:Castanea crenata|Chestnut]]), and fir ([[:en:Abies firma|Fir]]), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/parishioners|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 氏神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=ujigami|WD=Q767655}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Roof Raising Ceremony|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上棟式|1=raising ceremony|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q106351734}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, [[:en:Abbot (Buddhism)|Legitimate Abbot]] Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of [[:en:Illicium anisatum|Shikimi]], he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/carrying case|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 背負子|1=pack frame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q820964}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = [[:en:September 23|September 23]] |Rituals = |location = {{ill|Toyota|WD=Q201117}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.0535806|N|137.2830028|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shrine]] located in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]], [[:en:Toyota, Aichi|Toyota City]], {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakaue Town|1=Sakaue-chō, Toyota|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q131179285}}. Its former shrine Rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deities|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}} are [[:en:Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko]] (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シオツチオジ|1=Shiotsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11174872}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), [[:en:Kunado-no-Kami|Kunado-no-Kami]], and [[:en:Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru]] (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|Nagare-zukuri]] style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/copper-sheathed roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tiled roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瓦葺き|1=tiled roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10855730}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Festival Hall|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭文|1=saimon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17991683}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Procession Hall|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Haiden (Shinto)|Worship Hall]], and [[:en:Kagura-den|Kagura Hall]]; a [[:en:Stage (theatre)|Stage]] (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Office|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社|1=Shinto shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q845945}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Treasure House|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cedar-bark roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜皮葺|1=cypress bark roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q90373477}}; and the first, second, and third [[:en:Torii|Torii]], among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. (2012 (Heisei 24) April) [[ja:六所神社 (豊田市)]] == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November [[:en:2019|2019]] ([[:en:Reiwa era|Reiwa]] first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutou Mountain|1=Mount Sanage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11572109}} and [[:en:Mount Hongū (Aichi)|Hongu Mountain]]—as one of the three sacred mountains of [[:en:Mikawa Province|Mikawa Province]]. The mountain itself was revered as a [[:en:Shintai|Shintai]], and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ|1=Ōyamatsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q386563}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|1=Shinto architecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3080012}}—a notion derived from [[:en:Buddhism|Buddhism]]—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]; the discovery of fragments of [[:en:Earthenware|Earthenware]] (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]] in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rituals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭|1=festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q132241}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ([[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the [[:en:Typhoon Vera|Isewan Typhoon]] that struck in [[:en:September|September]] [[:en:1959|1959]] ([[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa]] 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira-go|1=Matsudairagō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11530613}}, the birthplace of the [[:en:Matsudaira clan|Matsudaira clan]] (from which the [[:en:Tokugawa clan|Tokugawa clan]] originated). On [[:en:August 19|August 19]] (old calendar) in [[:en:1377|1377]] ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiwa|1=Eiwa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11131293}} 3, [[:en:Tianshou|Tenju]] 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, [[:en:Matsudaira Chikauji|Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue]], is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of [[:en:Shiogama shrine|Shiogama Shrine]]) from [[:en:Mutsu Province|Ōshū]] onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ([[:en:Ubusunagami|Ubusunagami]]) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|末社|lt=Sessha|1=Setsumatsusha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Subsidiary Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guest Deity|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to まれびと|1=Marebito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6758746}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ([[:en:Ujigami|Ujigami]]) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as [[:en:1474|1474]] (the first year of the [[:en:Ōnin|Ōnin era]]), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Chikatada|1=Matsudaira Chikatada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11239171}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in [[:en:1520|1520]] (the first year of the [[:en:Eishō (Muromachi period)|Eishō era]]) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Nagachika|1=Matsudaira Nagachika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11239108}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December [[:en:1527|1527]] (the 7th year of the [[:en:Daiei (era)|Daiei era]]), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, [[:en:Matsudaira Nobutada|Matsudaira Nobutada]], jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Donation|1=contribution|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11455717}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazawa Town|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In [[:en:1542|1542]] (the 11th year of the [[:en:Tenbun|Tenmon]]), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, [[:en:Matsudaira Hirotada|Matsudaira Hirotada]], had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Legitimate Heir|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 嫡男|1=eldest Di son|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10102290}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day [[:en:Okazaki, Aichi|Okazaki City]] and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meidaiji Town|1=Myōdaijichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17216176}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of [[:en:Okazaki Castle|Okazaki Castle]]—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiroku period|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ([[:en:1558|1558]]–[[:en:1570|1570]]). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to [[:en:1546|1546]].『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze_Statue_of_Matsudaira_Chikauji,_Matsudaira-cho_Toyota_2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ([[:en:Reiwa era|Reiwa]] first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by [[:en:Kanō Tan'yū|Kano Tanyu]], housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Castle|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大坂城}}) }} After [[:en:1590|1590]] ([[:en:Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tenshō Era]] 18) when [[:en:Tokugawa Ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kantō|1=Kantō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11655841}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanaka Yoshimasa|1=Tanaka Yoshimasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11575390}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in [[:en:1602|1602]] ([[:en:Keichō|Keichō]] 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], in [[:en:1617|1617]] ([[:en:Genna|Genwa]] 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|1=Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q115587223}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of [[:en:Brown rice|Brown Rice]] was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In [[:en:1638|1638]] ([[:en:Kan'ei|Kan'ei]] 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Shigekazu|1=Matsudaira Shigefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6829219}}, again built the Main Hall. In [[:en:1667|1667]] ([[:en:Kanbun (era)|Kanbun]] 7), [[:en:1683|1683]] ([[:en:Tenna|Tennai]] 3), and [[:en:1686|1686]] ([[:en:Jōkyō|Jokyō]] 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the [[:en:Okutono Domain|Okudono-han]], {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikyū Matsudaira family|1=Ogyū-Matsudaira clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11260880}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noritsugu|1=Matsudaira Noritsugu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729484}}. From [[:en:1736|1736]] ([[:en:Genbun|Genbun]] 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Eijō|1=Matsudaira Mitsunori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729524}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In [[:en:1779|1779]] ([[:en:An'ei|An'ei]] 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noriomi|1=Matsudaira Noriyasu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729488}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In [[:en:1790|1790]] ([[:en:Kansei|Kansei]] 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Norito|1=Matsudaira Noritada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729477}}. In [[:en:1849|1849]] ([[:en:Kaei|Kaei]] 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fudō Ichiu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noritoshi|1=Matsudaira Noritoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729467}}. In [[:en:1858|1858]] ([[:en:Ansei|Ansei]] 5) and [[:en:1861|1861]] ([[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noriaki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大給恒|1=Matsudaira Norikata|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6788054}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In [[:en:1873|1873]] ([[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and in [[:en:1917|1917]] ([[:en:Taishō era|Taishō]] 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from [[:en:1918|1918]] (Taishō 7) to [[:en:1920|1920]] (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in [[:en:1921 (2021 film)|1921]] (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Agency|1=Jinja-cho|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11590703}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious Corporation|1=religious corporation|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7311343}} Rokusho Kami|ja|軻遇突智神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ|1=Kagu-tsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1640658}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on [[:en:February 15|February 15]], [[:en:1973|1973]] ([[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa]] 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in [[:en:1872|1872]] (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 [[:en:Ken (unit)|ken]] (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/beam|1=beam|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11538319}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/thatched roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 明治|1=Meiji period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3125096}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ([[:en:Cryptomeria|Japanese Cedar]]), cypress ([[:en:Chamaecyparis obtusa|Cypress]]), chestnut ([[:en:Castanea crenata|Chestnut]]), and fir ([[:en:Abies firma|Fir]]), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/parishioners|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 氏神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=ujigami|WD=Q767655}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Roof Raising Ceremony|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上棟式|1=raising ceremony|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q106351734}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, [[:en:Abbot (Buddhism)|Legitimate Abbot]] Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of [[:en:Illicium anisatum|Shikimi]], he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/carrying case|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 背負子|1=pack frame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q820964}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine

[Lower Shrine] Aichi Prefecture Toyota City Sakaue-cho, 23 Jizōdō |Coordinates = {{wikicoord|35|3|12.89|N|137|16|58.81|E}} "Upper Shrine"
{{wikicoord|35|3|49.90|N|137|16|14.44|E}} "Lower Shrine" |Deities = Sarutahiko no Kami
Kotokuni Katsunaga no Kami
{{ill|Kunado-no-Kami|en|Kunado-no-Kami|WD=Q2963653|lt=Kunado-no-Kami}}
{{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} |Rank = Prefectural Shrine |Founded = {{ill|1377|en|1377|WD=Q6289|lt=1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiwa|1=Eiwa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11131293}} 3, {{ill|Tianshou|en|Tianshou|WD=Q10939676|lt=Tenju}} 3) |Main Hall = [Upper Shrine] {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/copper-sheathed roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|en|September 23|WD=Q2888|lt=September 23}} |Rituals = |location = {{ill|Toyota|WD=Q201117}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.0535806|N|137.2830028|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shrine}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}, {{ill|Toyota, Aichi|en|Toyota, Aichi|WD=Q201117|lt=Toyota City}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakaue Town|1=Sakaue-chō, Toyota|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q131179285}}. Its former shrine Rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deities|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|Sarutahiko Ōkami|WD=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シオツチオジ|1=Shiotsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11174872}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Kunado-no-Kami|en|Kunado-no-Kami|WD=Q2963653|lt=Kunado-no-Kami}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/copper-sheathed roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tiled roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瓦葺き|1=tiled roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10855730}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Festival Hall|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭文|1=saimon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17991683}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Procession Hall|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|WD=Q3125745|lt=Worship Hall}}, and {{ill|Kagura-den|en|Kagura-den|WD=Q94498|lt=Kagura Hall}}; a {{ill|Stage (theatre)|en|Stage (theatre)|WD=Q194428|lt=Stage}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Office|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社|1=Shinto shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q845945}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Treasure House|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cedar-bark roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜皮葺|1=cypress bark roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q90373477}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=Torii}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|First Torii of Rokusho Shrine. In the background stands Rokusho Mountain.
({{ill|2019|en|2019|WD=Q25274|lt=2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|en|Reiwa era|WD=Q62609017|lt=Reiwa}} first year) November) Rokusho Jinja Jouku 02, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.jpg|Upper Shrine of Rokusho Shrine
({{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 24) April) Hachigamine Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Hachigamine Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) April) Rokusho Jinja Geku Haiden, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|Lower Shrine Worship Hall of Rokusho Shrine
(2019 (Reiwa first year) November) Jinguji Ato, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Site of Jinguji Hoshoji
(2012 (Heisei 24) April) [[ja:六所神社 (豊田市)]] == History == [[File:Distant View of Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|thumb|right|Distant view of Rokusho Mountain
(Sakaue-cho, Toyota, November {{ill|2019|en|2019|WD=Q25274|lt=2019}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|en|Reiwa era|WD=Q62609017|lt=Reiwa}} first year))]] Since ancient times, {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} has been regarded—together with {{ill|Sarutou Mountain|ja|猿投山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutou Mountain|1=Mount Sanage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11572109}} and {{ill|Mount Hongū (Aichi)|en|Mount Hongū (Aichi)|WD=Q211532|lt=Hongu Mountain}}—as one of the three sacred mountains of {{ill|Mikawa Province|en|Mikawa Province|WD=Q768158|lt=Mikawa Province}}. The mountain itself was revered as a {{ill|Shintai|en|Shintai|WD=Q327532|lt=Shintai}}, and six deities including {{ill|Ōyamatumi|ja|大山積神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ|1=Ōyamatsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q386563}} (Ōyamatumi) were enshrined.『松平町誌』：758-759ページ Even today, the first torii standing on the small plateau known as "Kinsen" is located at the most suitable spot for distant worship of Rokusho Mountain, suggesting that in ancient times the earliest distant worship site may have been established here.『坂上町誌』：10ページ Later, the concept of constructing a {{ill|Shrine Building|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|1=Shinto architecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3080012}}—a notion derived from {{ill|Buddhism|en|Buddhism|WD=Q748|lt=Buddhism}}—spread throughout the country, and it is believed that a shrine building was erected at the summit of Rokusho Mountain no later than the end of the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}; the discovery of fragments of {{ill|Earthenware|en|Earthenware|WD=Q1377111|lt=Earthenware}} (kawarake) dating from the Heian to the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|WD=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}} in the vicinity of the Upper Shrine further attests that rituals ({{ill|Rituals|ja|祭祀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rituals|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭|1=festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q132241}}) were once performed here.『坂上町誌』：10-11ページ Moreover, since the 1604 ({{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} 9) "Keichō Kenchichō" mentions a place called "Torii-shita", it is presumed that the first torii had already been constructed by that time; however, the precise date of its establishment remains uncertain. For a long time, giant pine trees stood on both sides of the torii, with both reportedly over 500 years old, but they were felled by the {{ill|Typhoon Vera|en|Typhoon Vera|WD=Q1060156|lt=Isewan Typhoon}} that struck in {{ill|September|en|September|WD=Q123|lt=September}} {{ill|1959|en|1959|WD=Q5302|lt=1959}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 34).『坂上町誌』：88ページ The area was once known as {{ill|Matsudaira-go|ja|松平郷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira-go|1=Matsudairagō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11530613}}, the birthplace of the {{ill|Matsudaira clan|en|Matsudaira clan|WD=Q1141077|lt=Matsudaira clan}} (from which the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|en|Tokugawa clan|WD=Q1412769|lt=Tokugawa clan}} originated). On {{ill|August 19|en|August 19|WD=Q2829|lt=August 19}} (old calendar) in {{ill|1377|en|1377|WD=Q6289|lt=1377}} ({{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiwa|1=Eiwa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11131293}} 3, {{ill|Tianshou|en|Tianshou|WD=Q10939676|lt=Tenju}} 3), the founding head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikauji|en|Matsudaira Chikauji|WD=Q11239169|lt=Matsudaira Tarōzaemon Chikaue}}, is said to have enshrined the deity Shiogama Rokusho Myōjin (the deity of the Rokusho palace of {{ill|Shiogama shrine|en|Shiogama shrine|WD=Q133753|lt=Shiogama Shrine}}) from {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Ōshū}} onto Rokusho Mountain. Until then the mountain had been known as "Yoshikiyama" or "Hachigamine-yama", but from then on it came to be called Rokusho Mountain. The tutelary deity ({{ill|Ubusunagami|en|Ubusunagami|WD=Q1392097|lt=Ubusunagami}}) formerly worshipped, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}}, ceded its sacred land and was relocated to the northeastern Hachigamine, thereafter continuing its existence as Hachigamine Shrine—a subsidiary shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|末社|lt=Sessha|1=Setsumatsusha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Subsidiary Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}}) of Rokusho Shrine—known as the "Retired Deity", while the newly enshrined main hall of the guest deity ({{ill|Guest Deity|ja|客人神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guest Deity|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to まれびと|1=Marebito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6758746}}), named Hōjuki Palace, came to be called Rokusho Daimyōjin and was venerated as the clan deity ({{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|WD=Q767655|lt=Ujigami}}) by successive heads of the Matsudaira and Tokugawa families.『松平町誌』：759ページ As early as {{ill|1474|en|1474|WD=Q6600|lt=1474}} (the first year of the {{ill|Ōnin|en|Ōnin|WD=Q1143903|lt=Ōnin era}}), the fourth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Chikatada|ja|松平親忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Chikatada|1=Matsudaira Chikatada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11239171}}, undertook the rebuilding of the shrine building, and in {{ill|1520|en|1520|WD=Q6284|lt=1520}} (the first year of the {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|en|Eishō (Muromachi period)|WD=Q1193577|lt=Eishō era}}) the fifth head, {{ill|Matsudaira Nagachika|ja|松平長親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Nagachika|1=Matsudaira Nagachika|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11239108}}, also worked on its reconstruction. In December {{ill|1527|en|1527|WD=Q6412|lt=1527}} (the 7th year of the {{ill|Daiei (era)|en|Daiei (era)|WD=Q1193564|lt=Daiei era}}), a wildfire completely burned the shrine building; at that time, Matsudaira Nagachika and the sixth head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobutada|en|Matsudaira Nobutada|WD=Q11239118|lt=Matsudaira Nobutada}}, jointly solicited donations ({{ill|Donation|ja|寄進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Donation|1=contribution|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11455717}}) from the Matsudaira clan for rebuilding the estate. Tradition holds that the Lower Shrine—originally located in Makigata Kawamura (present-day {{ill|Hanazawa Town|ja|花沢町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanazawa Town|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Toyota City) at the southern foot of Rokusho Mountain—was later relocated to its current site and the area renamed Miyaguchi Village by Matsudaira Nagachika.『坂上町誌』：245ページ In {{ill|1542|en|1542|WD=Q6520|lt=1542}} (the 11th year of the {{ill|Tenbun|en|Tenbun|WD=Q1192853|lt=Tenmon}}), when the 8th head of the Matsudaira family, {{ill|Matsudaira Hirotada|en|Matsudaira Hirotada|WD=Q1064935|lt=Matsudaira Hirotada}}, had his legitimate heir ({{ill|Legitimate Heir|ja|嫡子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Legitimate Heir|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 嫡男|1=eldest Di son|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10102290}}) Taketoyo born, worship was reportedly conducted at the Rokusho Shrine in Takamiya Village (present-day {{ill|Okazaki, Aichi|en|Okazaki, Aichi|WD=Q242783|lt=Okazaki City}} and {{ill|Meidaiji Town|ja|明大寺町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meidaiji Town|1=Myōdaijichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17216176}}); later, Taketoyo—who became lord of {{ill|Okazaki Castle|en|Okazaki Castle|WD=Q1013445|lt=Okazaki Castle}}—is said to have enshrined three of the six deities of Rokusho Daimyōjin during the {{ill|Eiroku period|ja|Eiroku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiroku period|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{ill|1558|en|1558|WD=Q6601|lt=1558}}–{{ill|1570|en|1570|WD=Q6659|lt=1570}}). However, according to the Okazaki City Chronicle and historical documents such as Matsudaira Hirotada’s donation letter, it appears that the relocation had already occurred prior to {{ill|1546|en|1546|WD=Q6533|lt=1546}}.『角川日本地名大辞典 23 愛知県』：1416ページ {{right| Bronze_Statue_of_Matsudaira_Chikauji,_Matsudaira-cho_Toyota_2019.jpg|Portrait of Matsudaira Chikaue
(Matsudaira Town, Toyota City, August 2019 ({{ill|Reiwa era|en|Reiwa era|WD=Q62609017|lt=Reiwa}} first year)) Tokugawa Ieyasu2.JPG|Portrait of Tokugawa Ieyasu
(Painting by {{ill|Kanō Tan'yū|en|Kanō Tan'yū|WD=Q961405|lt=Kano Tanyu}}, housed in the keep of {{ill|Osaka Castle|ja|大阪城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Castle|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大坂城}}) }} After {{ill|1590|en|1590|WD=Q6764|lt=1590}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|WD=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} 18) when {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|WD=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} was transferred to the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kantō|1=Kantō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11655841}} region, he came under the rule of Okazaki Castle’s lord {{ill|Tanaka Yoshimasa|ja|田中吉政|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanaka Yoshimasa|1=Tanaka Yoshimasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11575390}} and had his temple and shrine lands confiscated; however, in {{ill|1602|en|1602|WD=Q6727|lt=1602}} ({{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|WD=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} 7) he was granted an initial offering of 20 koku of rice for Rokusho Daimyōjin by Tokugawa Ieyasu. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, in {{ill|1617|en|1617|WD=Q6798|lt=1617}} ({{ill|Genna|en|Genna|WD=Q635245|lt=Genwa}} 3) the 8th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|ja|松平由重|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|1=Matsudaira Yoshi-shige|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q115587223}}, constructed the Main Hall, and simultaneously, 4 koku 7 to 8 shō 3 gō of {{ill|Brown rice|en|Brown rice|WD=Q1066624|lt=Brown Rice}} was exempted as the annual festival and lantern fee from Miyaguchi Village.『松平町誌』：760ページ In {{ill|1638|en|1638|WD=Q6893|lt=1638}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|WD=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei}} 15), the 10th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Shigekazu|ja|松平重和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Shigekazu|1=Matsudaira Shigefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6829219}}, again built the Main Hall. In {{ill|1667|en|1667|WD=Q7588|lt=1667}} ({{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|WD=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun}} 7), {{ill|1683|en|1683|WD=Q7651|lt=1683}} ({{ill|Tenna|en|Tenna|WD=Q1145289|lt=Tennai}} 3), and {{ill|1686|en|1686|WD=Q7664|lt=1686}} ({{ill|Jōkyō|en|Jōkyō|WD=Q1146221|lt=Jokyō}} 4), the buildings were rebuilt and renovated by the first head of the {{ill|Okutono Domain|en|Okutono Domain|WD=Q3034400|lt=Okudono-han}}, {{ill|Daikyū Matsudaira family|ja|大給松平家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daikyū Matsudaira family|1=Ogyū-Matsudaira clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11260880}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritsugu|ja|松平乗次|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noritsugu|1=Matsudaira Noritsugu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729484}}. From {{ill|1736|en|1736|WD=Q6989|lt=1736}} ({{ill|Genbun|en|Genbun|WD=Q1145754|lt=Genbun}} 1) to the following year, the buildings were reconstructed by the 4th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Eijō|ja|松平盈乗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Eijō|1=Matsudaira Mitsunori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729524}}. There were also donations of 2 koku 4 to of brown rice as lantern fees and exemptions of 7 to 8 shō 3 gō as annual festival fees. In {{ill|1779|en|1779|WD=Q7714|lt=1779}} ({{ill|An'ei|en|An'ei|WD=Q1193910|lt=An'ei}} 8), the buildings were constructed by the 5th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriomi|ja|松平乗穏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noriomi|1=Matsudaira Noriyasu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729488}}.『松平町誌』：761ページ In {{ill|1790|en|1790|WD=Q7775|lt=1790}} ({{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|WD=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} 2), they were built by the 7th generation of that family, {{ill|Matsudaira Norito|ja|松平乗尹|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Norito|1=Matsudaira Noritada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729477}}. In {{ill|1849|en|1849|WD=Q7650|lt=1849}} ({{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|WD=Q1146125|lt=Kaei}} 2), the Lower Shrine saw the construction of the {{ill|Fudō Ichiu|ja|不動一宇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fudō Ichiu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} by the 9th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noritoshi|ja|松平乗利|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noritoshi|1=Matsudaira Noritoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10729467}}. In {{ill|1858|en|1858|WD=Q7684|lt=1858}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|WD=Q1327259|lt=Ansei}} 5) and {{ill|1861|en|1861|WD=Q7693|lt=1861}} ({{ill|Bunkyū|en|Bunkyū|WD=Q730266|lt=Bunkyū}} 2), the Main Hall was reconstructed and repaired and the torii were rebuilt by the 10th generation of the Daikyū Matsudaira family of Okudono-han, {{ill|Matsudaira Noriaki|ja|松平乗謨|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Noriaki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大給恒|1=Matsudaira Norikata|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6788054}}, together with the 16th generation of the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, {{ill|Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja|松平頼載|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Yoriyori|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The benevolence shown by the Tokugawa and Matsudaira clans—in particular, by the Daikyū Matsudaira family, lords of Miyaguchi Village, and the Matsudaira Tarōzaemon family, rulers of Matsudaira-go—is beyond enumeration. In {{ill|1873|en|1873|WD=Q7757|lt=1873}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 6) the name of Rokusho Daimyōjin was changed to '''Rokusho Shrine'''. Its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and in {{ill|1917|en|1917|WD=Q2092|lt=1917}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|WD=Q329174|lt=Taishō}} 6) the divestment of the shrine-owned forest on Rokusho Mountain (which had been designated as a government forest) was approved; from {{ill|1918|en|1918|WD=Q2094|lt=1918}} (Taishō 7) to {{ill|1920|en|1920|WD=Q2155|lt=1920}} (Taishō 9) the Lower Shrine’s Worship Hall and Festival Hall were rebuilt, and in {{ill|1921 (2021 film)|en|1921 (2021 film)|WD=Q107356491|lt=1921}} (Taishō 10) it was elevated to a Prefectural Shrine. It now belongs to the Aichi Prefecture {{ill|Shrine Agency|ja|神社庁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Agency|1=Jinja-cho|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11590703}} and is registered as the religious corporation {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious Corporation|1=religious corporation|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7311343}} Rokusho Shrine.『坂上町誌』：237-238ページ == Major Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|WD=Q2150|lt=January 1}}: {{ill|New Year's Festival|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/New Year's Festival|1=Saitan-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11546824}} * {{ill|February 11|en|February 11|WD=Q2335|lt=February 11}}: Foundation Festival * {{ill|February 17|en|February 17|WD=Q2341|lt=February 17}}: {{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|WD=Q118906710|lt=Harvest Festival}}, Akiba Shrine Festival, Mountain Deity Festival * {{ill|June 30|en|June 30|WD=Q2657|lt=June 30}}: {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|en|Ōharae-shiki|WD=Q11261910|lt=Great Purification}} * {{ill|July 25|en|July 25|WD=Q2720|lt=July 25}}: Hachigamine Shrine Festival * {{ill|September 1|en|September 1|WD=Q2859|lt=September 1}}: 210th Day Festival, Atsuta Festival * {{ill|September 22|en|September 22|WD=Q2889|lt=September 22}}: Deity Welcoming Ritual and Eve Festival * {{ill|September 23|en|September 23|WD=Q2888|lt=September 23}}: {{ill|Annual Festival|ja|例祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Annual Festival|1=reisai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11385469}} and Deity Sending-off Ritual * {{ill|November 23|en|November 23|WD=Q3021|lt=November 23}}: {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|WD=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai}} * {{ill|December 31|en|December 31|WD=Q2912|lt=December 31}}: Great Purification and New Year's Eve Festival * Every 1st of the month: {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} == Subordinate Shrines == * {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Upper Shrine): Ōyamatsumi (commonly known as “Retired Deity”) * {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}} (Lower Shrine): {{ill|Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja|軻遇突智神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakugutsuchi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ|1=Kagu-tsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1640658}} == Others == === Rokusho Shrine Stage === This stage is designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City. It was designated on {{ill|February 15|en|February 15|WD=Q2334|lt=February 15}}, {{ill|1973|en|1973|WD=Q2477|lt=1973}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 48) and is managed by Rokusho Shrine. Built in {{ill|1872|en|1872|WD=Q7753|lt=1872}} (Meiji 5) within the precincts of the Lower Shrine, this wooden, single‐story, thatched stage has a frontage of 8 {{ill|Ken (unit)|en|Ken (unit)|WD=Q3195007|lt=ken}} (14.5 meters) and a depth of 4.7 ken (8.5 meters).[http://www.toyota-rekihaku.com/bunka/11_yuukei/win/03.html Rokusho Shrine Stage] (Toyota City Local History Museum website, viewed April 2, 2012) Of this, the stage’s 12.6‑meter frontage is continuously supported by a single thick {{ill|beam|ja|梁 (建築)|lt=Beam|lt_ja=梁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/beam|1=beam|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11538319}} (90 cm × 60 cm), and its roof is supported by a beam spanning the midpoint of the {{ill|thatched roof|ja|合掌材|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/thatched roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Inside, a mechanism known as the "double rigging"—which lifts performers up and down—is said to exemplify the archaic style of the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 明治|1=Meiji period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3125096}}. The timber, including Japanese cedar ({{ill|Cryptomeria|en|Cryptomeria|WD=Q147388|lt=Japanese Cedar}}), cypress ({{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|en|Chamaecyparis obtusa|WD=Q917187|lt=Cypress}}), chestnut ({{ill|Castanea crenata|en|Castanea crenata|WD=Q717827|lt=Chestnut}}), and fir ({{ill|Abies firma|en|Abies firma|WD=Q1718147|lt=Fir}}), was felled on Rokusho Mountain, and many local {{ill|parishioners|ja|氏子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/parishioners|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 氏神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=ujigami|WD=Q767655}} helped transport the materials, reportedly carving the rock outcrops when the timber encountered them.From the local information board. Moreover, during the {{ill|Roof Raising Ceremony|ja|棟上げ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Roof Raising Ceremony|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上棟式|1=raising ceremony|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q106351734}}, numerous spectators gathered from early morning, making for a very lively event.『松平町誌』：812ページ === Korokusho Shrine === It is located in the Furusha area of Sakaue Town (formerly Matsudaira Town, Sodame). ({{wikicoord|35|4|10.1|N|137|14|55.5|E|scale:2500|Coordinates}}) This is a small stone shrine belonging to the subordinate shrines of Shinmeisha. According to the Ancient Record Collection of {{ill|Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja|妙昌寺 (豊田市)|lt=Ōyanayama Myōchōji|lt_ja=大簗山妙昌寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyanayama Myōchōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, when the third abbot of Myōchōji, {{ill|Abbot (Buddhism)|en|Abbot (Buddhism)|WD=Q1135621|lt=Legitimate Abbot}} Muzen Yūrō (むぜんゆうりょう) entered Yanayama (present-day) in search of {{ill|Illicium anisatum|en|Illicium anisatum|WD=Q27019|lt=Shikimi}}, he encountered an elderly man resting with his {{ill|carrying case|ja|笈|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/carrying case|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 背負子|1=pack frame|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q820964}} draped over a pine tree. When the abbot inquired of him, the old man replied that he was the {{ill|Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja|奥州鹽竈明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshū Shiogama Myōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, explaining that he had come on an errand to protect the local parishioners and advising him to choose a place to settle before vanishing like smoke.From the local information board.『松平町誌』：779-780ページ Korokusho Jinja, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Korokusho Shrine
(2012 (Heisei 24) March) Myoushou-ji, Outaki-cho Toyota 2012.JPG|Ōyanayama Myōchōji

[Lower Shrine] Nagare-zukuri {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}} |Alternative names = |Other designations = |Annual Festival = {{ill|September 23|en|September 23|WD=Q2888|lt=September 23}} |Rituals = |location = {{ill|Toyota|WD=Q201117}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.0535806|N|137.2830028|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' (六所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shrine}} located in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}, {{ill|Toyota, Aichi|en|Toyota, Aichi|WD=Q201117|lt=Toyota City}}, {{ill|Sakaue Town|ja|坂上町 (豊田市)|lt=Sakaue Town|lt_ja=坂上町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakaue Town|1=Sakaue-chō, Toyota|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q131179285}}. Its former shrine Rank was {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Overview == It is also the collective name for the shrine complex composed of the Upper Shrine, {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the Lower Shrine. The {{ill|Enshrined Deities|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deities|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}} are {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|Sarutahiko Ōkami|WD=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko}} (【Sarutahiko】), {{ill|Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja|シオツチノオジ|lt=Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|lt_ja=塩椎神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シオツチオジ|1=Shiotsuchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11174872}} (【Shio-tsuchi-no-Oji】), {{ill|Kunado-no-Kami|en|Kunado-no-Kami|WD=Q2963653|lt=Kunado-no-Kami}}, and {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} (【Yamato Takeru no Mikoto】). The complex is comprised of a Main Hall constructed in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|WD=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} style with a {{ill|copper-sheathed roof|ja|銅板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/copper-sheathed roof|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a Secondary Hall converted from an old lodge (Upper Shrine), a provisional Main Hall in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|plank roof|ja|板葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/plank roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杮葺|1=wood shingle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q199388}}, a wooden, copper-sheathed Secondary Hall, and a set of wooden single‐story, {{ill|tiled roof|ja|瓦葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tiled roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瓦葺き|1=tiled roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10855730}} structures including the {{ill|Festival Hall|ja|祭文殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Festival Hall|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祭文|1=saimon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17991683}}, {{ill|Procession Hall|ja|渡殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Procession Hall|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|WD=Q3125745|lt=Worship Hall}}, and {{ill|Kagura-den|en|Kagura-den|WD=Q94498|lt=Kagura Hall}}; a {{ill|Stage (theatre)|en|Stage (theatre)|WD=Q194428|lt=Stage}} (designated as a tangible folk cultural property by Toyota City); a shrine office built in Nagare-zukuri wooden single‐story tiled style ({{ill|Shrine Office|ja|社務所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Office|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社|1=Shinto shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q845945}}); a shrine treasure house ({{ill|Shrine Treasure House|ja|神庫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine Treasure House|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}); the Main Hall of {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}} in the Lower Shrine built in Nagare-zukuri style with a copper-sheathed roof; the Main Hall of {{ill|Hachigamine Shrine|ja|八ケ峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachigamine Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} built in Nagare-zukuri style with a {{ill|cedar-bark roof|ja|桧皮葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/cedar-bark roof|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 檜皮葺|1=cypress bark roof|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q90373477}}; and the first, second, and third {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=Torii}}, among other structures.『坂上町誌』：242-243ページ The Upper Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain near the summit of {{ill|Rokusho Mountain|ja|六所山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Mountain|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Hachigamine Shrine lies just a little to its north, the Lower Shrine is sited in the Jizōdō area of Sakaue Town, and the first torii stands in the Kinsen area of Sakaue Town. Rokusho-Jinja Shrine Torii & Mount Rokusho, Sakaue-cho Toyota 2019.jpg|First Torii of Rokusho Shrine. In the background stands Rokusho Mountain.
